verdict.rationale: Fellow documents a REST Developer API that returns transcripts (recordings with diarized, timestamped transcripts via the `include` parameter), structured notes and meeting recaps, and action items through paginated list endpoints. Users generate their own named API keys. Two caveats limit the score: the API requires a paid plan and an admin-enabled workspace setting, and workspace-wide access to every meeting needs Enterprise Super Admin keys. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of the summary field in API responses, independent or hands-on corroboration, and access that is not gated by plan or admin.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my scripts can pull transcripts, summaries, and action items from every meeting through a documented API with self-serve keys

citations.quote: The Developer API opens that data to you: transcripts, structured notes, and more, all available through standard REST calls.
A Recording represents a meeting recap in Fellow, and associated metadata. Each Recording is associated with a Note, and can contain information such as: Diarized and timestamped transcripts
List action items with optional filters and pagination.
Generate a new API key for your application, giving it a descriptive name. You can have multiple API keys, and we recommend generating a different one for each application
pass transcripts to an LLM for tailored recaps and action plans, the API gives you everything you need to make it happen.
